detail:
The International Foundation for Gastrointestinal Disorders (IFFGD) describes itself as a nonprofit education and research organization whose mission is to inform, assist, and support people affected by gastrointestinal disorders. Through its Nancy and Bill Norton Research Program, IFFGD reports that it recognizes and supports scientists whose work advances the understanding, diagnosis, and treatment of gastrointestinal conditions, including functional gastrointestinal and motility disorders, the group of disorders in which GERD and related reflux conditions are studied.

IFFGD reports that its research program includes research grants for innovative projects, preceptorship awards for early-career clinicians, and travel awards for young investigators, and that dozens of researchers worldwide have been honored with its research awards and grants. Funded work described by the foundation aims at improvements in understanding gastrointestinal disorders, their pathophysiology, and the care of patients. IFFGD presents the program as support for early-career investigators active in basic or clinical research within its portfolio, rather than as a new treatment for any single condition.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about GERD research and research programs.
summary: IFFGD describes its Nancy and Bill Norton Research Program as funding grants, preceptorships, and travel awards for researchers advancing understanding, diagnosis, and treatment of gastrointestinal disorders, including the functional and motility disorders studied alongside GERD.
takeaways: iffgd funds gi research through its norton research program
grants support early-career basic and clinical investigators
the program funds research broadly, not a single gerd treatment
title: GERD: research support through the IFFGD research program
